Change has been successfully rebased and submitted as 9cb4abfce611bb8a2e625e006a6a18242a7fdef6

Can we add more of the "why" here also?  I think I heard that while the processor is turning on, the i3c connection is not stable and can cause spurious data.  Waiting until after the processor is active resolves this.
Done
Hi @patrick@stwcx.xyz, could you help to review this change? Thanks!
Since we are going to 'stop' this, there is a minor change need to the service file I think... will leave a comment there.
Done
Let's move this into the `bind-apml-driver` itself (I left comments elsewhere).
Done
It really takes 2 minutes before we can use the i3c line reliably?  This seems extraordinarily long...
Acknowledged

I think we need `RemainAfterExit=true` here also.  This keeps the service as "active" even after it runs so that:

1. You can 'stop' it.
2. It will only run a single time.

See I00669e3acda1f7d0f6a44b524084b7a8ca9919d2 for some additional learning as to why this is preferred.
Done

I'd prefer if you have this script ran as `bind-apml-driver on` and `bind-apml-driver off` for the ExecStart and ExecStop respectively.  Then we can keep all the on/off bind/unbind calls in a single place.
Done
Do we need to stop the service here also?  Would prefer we refactor this to always stop the service here.
Done
Do we actually need 2 minutes of sleep?  I asked this on an earlier patch set.
We have checked the bus signal analyzer, 2 minutes will be safer.
Checking if the 2min delay would cause any impact from the DC tooling perspective.
Could we know which tooling function might be impact?
LGTM

Discussed with Albin Cheng and functional impact is:
BMC cannot obtain the CPU/DIMM temperature sensors on power-on. Need to wait for ~2 mins for CPU to stabilize and avoid sending garbage packets to BMC via the I3C interface. 

This issue is being root-caused by AMD in https://ontrack.amd.com/browse/FBA-720 Meanwhile, this issue is mitigated by delaying the I3C driver bind for 120 seconds
